subject.title: Add maxThreads config for local embedding (node-llama-cpp)

question: Should OpenClaw officially expose `memorySearch.local.maxThreads` for the llama.cpp local embedding provider, or keep CPU thread tuning outside canonical config?
rationale: The requested option is dependency-backed and mechanically small, but it creates a new public config surface for local embedding performance/resource control.

options.title: Approve narrow maxThreads knob
options.body: Add an optional advanced field, leave the default undefined, and forward it only to `getLlama` for the official local provider.

options.title: Reject config expansion
options.body: Keep current local embedding defaults and direct deeper CPU tuning to external providers, custom plugins, or future provider-owned configuration.

options.title: Defer to broader local tuning design
options.body: Hold this until maintainers decide a larger local llama tuning surface for threads, GPU, NUMA, and related runtime options.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow maxThreads knob
recommendation.body: Add an optional advanced field, leave the default undefined, and forward it only to `getLlama` for the official local provider.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the core config schema, memory resolver, and official llama.cpp provider boundary where recent history points to Peter Steinberger.
